sample_unit: physicians (20 residents, 5 attendings; 225 vignette responses) plus 8 LLMs (144 outputs)
models_evaluated: eight LLMs (specific models not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic ranking shift when a misleading patient statement (anchor) was added to vignettes
links.effect: LLMs ranked the anchor first in 55.6% of responses vs 21.2% (residents) and 10.0% (attendings); anchor in top-5 in 97.2% of LLM outputs; Borda shift 2.29 (LLMs) vs 0.88 (residents).
links.quote: In anchored vignettes, residents ranked the anchor first in 17/80 responses (21.2%) and attendings in 2/20 (10.0%), compared with LLMs in 40/72 responses (55.6%).

links.outcome: Susceptibility of LLMs to anchoring bias in diagnostic ranking compared with physicians
links.effect: LLMs had higher odds of ranking the anchor first versus residents (OR 3.94, 95% CI 2.32-7.33) and attendings (OR 4.07, 95% CI 2.47-7.21).
links.quote: LLMs had higher odds of ranking the anchor first versus residents (OR 3.94, 95% CI 2.32-7.33; P < 0.001) and attendings (OR 4.07, 95% CI 2.47-7.21; P < 0.001).

screen.reason: Empirical study comparing diagnostic anchoring bias between LLMs and clinicians on clinical vignettes; it evaluates model behavior/safety vulnerability rather than testing a specific implementation safeguard.
